notes: 'which' is added: the Hebrew writes the antecedent and no relative morpheme stands in the clause, so rule 46's closing clause hands it to rules 30 and 55 rather than licensing it.
'for their clothing' is read as the ASV's recasting of the verbless clause's copular relation onto לְבוּשָׁם; the competing reading marks 'for' added, and is named on that unit.
כֻּלָּם is segmented with reversed glosses in the packet; the alignment follows the surface and morphology (rule 39), giving 'all' to כֹּל and the subject pronoun 'they' to the suffix (rules 18, 40).
